**Good news – we can get your pet‑photo app up and running quickly.** It looks like you want a place where people can: 1. **Upload photos of their pets.** 2. **Other users can like those photos.** Since people will be interacting with each other’s content, we need logins and some basic database rules to keep each user’s own uploads private until they’re liked. That’s an **Amber**‑level project (logins + personal data + interactions). --- ## Starter questions (short, one line each) 1. Who will use the app? (just you & close friends, general public, a club, etc.) 2. Will users sign up with an email link (magic link) or a different method? 3. Do you already have a Lovable project set up, or should we create one from scratch? 4. Do you have a Supabase account ready (or should I guide you through creating one)? Answering these will let us pick the safest defaults and keep the plan focused. --- ## Quick safety checklist for this feature | Feature | Safety parts we’ll build in | |---------|-----------------------------| | Photo uploads | • Users can only add/delete their own files
• Only image types (.jpg/.png) up to 5 MB
• Files stored in a private Supabase bucket | | Likes | • Users can only like or unlike their own or others’ photos
• Database row‑level security so each user sees only their own likes | | Logins | • Magic‑link sign‑in via Supabase Auth (no passwords needed) | | Secrets | • Supabase keys stored in the platform’s Secrets registry, never in frontend code | --- ## Next steps Once you answer the questions, we’ll: 1. **Create or open your Lovable project** and set up a Supabase backend. 2. **Add the photo‑upload page** with a file input that checks type/size client‑side and sends it to Supabase Storage. 3. **Create a “photos” table** (id, user_id, bucket_path, created_at). Add RLS policies so only the owner can delete their own photos. 4. **Add a “likes” table** (user_id, photo_id). Add RLS so users can only like/unlike a photo once and only read their own likes. 5. **Show a feed** of all uploaded photos with like buttons; the button will toggle a record in the “likes” table. 6. **Add safety proofs**: A quick test that a user can upload, see their photo, and that another user cannot delete it. 7. **Save points**: After each step, we’ll snapshot the project so you can roll back if anything goes wrong. --- ### Do you want to start a new project or work on an existing Lovable app? Pick the quickest route for you, and we’ll dive in.
